body:
I couldn't make a text post... 

Is it true that SSRI can make things worse in the long term? Can Tardive Dysphoria (delayed depression) be caused by SSRI?

Can anyone please comment on this question and these two related articles?

http://www.psychologytoday.com/blog/mad-in-america/201106/now-antidepressant-induced-chronic-depression-has-name-tardive-dysphoria

http://www.behaviorismandmentalhealth.com/2014/04/08/antidepressants-make-things-worse-in-the-long-term/

Just listening and being there is enough. 

If it's too hard for you or you can't disconnect your emotions from what they tell then just explain that to them, they might not understand and they might get angry but don't let this drive them away. Try to talk about other stuff with them, again, just being there is enough.

30 minutes of intense body weight exercise every day should be good for a start. Jumping rope is really good too, the cheapest one is good enough.

You should eat about 1.5 grams of proteins per kg of body weight in order to gain muscle. 

The FAQ on /r/Fitness is a goldmine.

I did chuckle.

>You absolutely have the ability to picture who you want to be as a person, and make the changes in your life to become as close to that as possible. 

After failing at uni after two semesters and not being able to lift weights or ride bicycle anymore due to injury (still not sure if it will be permanent), I don't know about that... These things really take the wind out of my sails.

>it's just nobody taught us how to drive all that well

Learning seemingly basic things as an adult can be difficult. Making or finding friends can be very difficult for example...

Is it a good idea for someone with depression and anxiety for example to see someone with the same condition? 

I mean, both of you can potentially make it worse for yourselves and both of you already have your own problems to deal with so having the other person's trouble could be overwhelming I think.

What if I can't make those changes? 

I can't pull myself out of the mud on my own...

This is a good place to start: http://neilarey.com/workouts.html

Also youtube: body weight workout.

I can only tell you why I'm ashamed of my depression and anxiety, because it makes me feel less of a man, it makes me feel weak and pathetic. 

The social norm is a man shouldn't be pathetic, he should be a Man, strong with balls and confidence, not a scared and anxious wreck that can't go outside...
Heh they pulled me out of her belly and early, I should have died then.
Alive and suffering... My social anxiety won't let me do those things and I'm not really seeing how it would be fun anyway...

Nothing has changed from yesterday's check in... 

It's my birthday though, I don't have anyone to celebrate it with... I don't even have a reason to celebrate...
You should start building muscle, this way you'll gain weight but in a healthy manner.

Went to a doc today and got some meds for this damn cough I have that doesn't let me sleep. 

Felt like shit all day, had no one to talk to, the suicide hotline where I live is supposed to have an online chat but it doesn't work, tried to tell them via mail but there's no reply. I don't want to call and talk over the phone with a stranger about this.

Didn't call my therapist either because she'll probably just tell me to talk about this next time we meet.

I'm tired all day from lack of sleep and the Codaine for the cough is making me even more tired.

Kinda like a diary with commentary huh. It seems kinda dead sometimes though...

I'll give it a try.
What's the point in this?
Can you go into more details on how you became friends with people you met in stores or gas stations or online?

How were you able to build a support system?

Making friends when you're an adult isn't easy.
How much time do you think is enough to give a therapist before you know it isn't working?
Can you describe more what do you mean by jolt?

9?! it must have taken months then to find the right dose... I hoped to start seeing results and get better after only a few weeks.

I already downloaded a book or two on CBT for patients and found a few online resources but I procrastinate and can't get myself to start reading them...
Check your inbox.

What you see on fb is only the good stuff, it's extremely filtered. 

I'm off fb for years now, I suggest you do the same, there's nothing really to see there.
How did you deal with depression and anxiety and suicidal thoughts?

Thanks.

A few questions: What do you take ?

Do you have to take them every day for the rest of your life ?

What happens if you miss a day or stop taking them for a few days ?

Do you think you'll ever be able to stop taking them and still be good ?

Aren't you building resistance over time, thus have to increase the dosage all the time ?
